topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the scope of the lecture series, and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Origins and Risk Factors of Cancer: Genetics, Chance, and Environment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer etiology, comparing the roles of intrinsic cellular mutations, genetic inheritance, chance, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral and bacterial infections contribute to oncogenesis, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical, Physical, and Promotional Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical and cellular mechanisms through which environmental agents cause DNA damage, require metabolic activation, or act as tumor promoters.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect carcinogenic exposure and evaluate mutagenic activity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing on evaluating the everyday risks and benefits of carcinogenic exposures.
